summary: Timebound cross-cloud read-only access for org-wide audit automation
description:
Issue summary:
Support is requested to provision timebound, least-privilege, cross-cloud read-only access for the Security Automation team to run an org-wide compliance/audit scan. The automation runs a set of read-only checks across AWS and GCP accounts (prod and staging) and requires the ability to enumerate IAM bindings, list S3/GCS buckets, and pull recent logs (CloudWatch / Cloud Logging) for the past 30 days.

Impact:
- Automation required by Compliance (internal) cannot complete until access is available; this blocks a scheduled control test for next week.
- Not providing timebound, auditable access increases risk around ad-hoc broad permissions.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Provision an ephemeral AWS IAM role and a mapped GCP service account access pattern usable by the automation runner.
- Access must be strictly read-only across specified projects/accounts: prod and staging (see environment field).
- Access TTL: 8 hours per issuance, issued via STS / Workload Identity; no long-lived credentials.
- All assumes/issuances must be logged (CloudTrail + Cloud Logging) and a short summary posted to #security-ops.
- Terraform changes must be captured in infra repo PRs listed above and linked to this ticket.

Environment / scope:
- AWS org: core-prod, core-staging (us-east region primary)
- GCP org: redwood-prod, redwood-staging (eu-west project group)
- Systems: S3, CloudWatch (Log Insights), IAM, GCS, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager (projects)

Steps to reproduce / how automation will use access:
1) Security automation pod (k8s) will exchange its short-lived pod identity for the ephemeral access via STS/Workload Identity and run inventory scripts.
2) Scripts call list/describe APIs only; no write/modify operations.

Requested TTL and justifications:
- TTL 8 hours to allow full scan without re-authorization.
- Timebound issuance reduces blast radius and supports auditability.

Approval chain / business justification:
- Approved by: Security (Maya R.) and Compliance (Evan R.).
- Business reason: required quarterly control test and evidence collection for SOC2 readiness.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Lydia Chen: Filing per Security ask (Maya). Need cross-cloud read-only access for automation run scheduled 2026-03-15. Prefer 8h TTL. Linking compliance request in Slack: #security -> thread t12345.
2026-03-10 11:03 - Diego Morales (CloudOps): Acknowledged. Will validate account lists and org policies. Can you paste the exact account IDs / project IDs?
2026-03-10 11:20 - Lydia Chen: Provided account/project list in attached Slack thread and confluence page. Also confirmed no write operations required — read-only inventory only.

2026-03-11 15:45 - Diego Morales (CloudOps): Preliminary checks: org SCPs in AWS block s3:ListAllMyBuckets at org-level unless conditioned; will use role with explicit s3:ListBucket on project buckets. In GCP, need workload identity pool mapping; creating PR for terraform changes.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Security (Maya R.): Confirmed approval for 8h TTL and audit logging requirement. Security requests conditional on MFA-backed assume or token issuing from internal STS gateway.
2026-03-12 17:02 - Diego Morales: Created infra PRs and applied to staging once approved. Will schedule role issuance test tomorrow morning and notify #security-ops with logs link.
investigation_notes: Checked org SCPs and IAM conditions in AWS - existing org-level deny prevents broad s3:ListAllMyBuckets; will create resource-level allow for listed bucket ARNs.
GCP projects use centralized KMS and audit logs are routed to a logging-bucket; will ensure service account has logging.viewer and storage.objectViewer scoped roles only.
Validated that the automation runner can use workload identity federation to assume AWS role via OIDC proxy; implemented external ID pattern to prevent confused-deputy.
Confirmed CloudTrail and Cloud Logging retention is sufficient for 30-day evidence; added extra event logging for AssumeRole and key service calls for this TTL window.
Applied least-privilege principle: no iam:PutRolePolicy or iam:PassRole; restricted to sts:AssumeRole and read-only API sets.
resolution:
In-progress rollout: Created AWS role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ephemeral-audit-readonly with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRole from the internal STS gateway (external-id in place). Created GCP service account redwood-ephemeral-audit@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and mapped to a workload identity pool for the automation runner. Terraform PRs: infra/pull/2387 and terraform-cloud/pull/166 contain the exact policy bundles.

Testing notes: Applied to staging 2026-03-12, successful assume-role end-to-end and inventory run completed with only read operations. Logs were forwarded to the compliance logging bucket and an audit summary posted to #security-ops.

Follow-ups before closing:
- Roll the change to prod after one more smoke test (assigned to Diego).
- Add automated TTL issuance to the internal STS gateway (ticket INT-16010) and link back.
- Add an Ops-runbook snippet to Confluence: Cross-Cloud Ephemeral Access (pending PR).

Ticket will be updated when prod rollout is complete and PRs are merged.
